description:
FILED s462as (round 19), with the discriminating measurement already taken â
but taken on a LOADED machine, which is why this is a task and not a change.

THE OBSERVATION.  `cl/pcl-runtime.lisp`'s only `(declaim (optimize â¦))` is at
the very END of the file (line ~20958, `(speed 2) (safety 1) (debug 0)`), and a
declaim at the end of a file applies to what is compiled AFTER it â i.e. to the
GENERATED program, not to the runtime's own 20k lines.  The runtime therefore
compiles at SBCL's default policy (speed 1 / safety 1 / debug 1), and it is the
runtime that every PCL program spends its time in.

WHY IT IS WORTH ASKING NOW.  #922 (s462as) found that `%p-fixnum-string`'s
digit loops were GENERIC truncate calls, one full call per digit â not because
of policy, but because one declared type was one value too wide.  That is the
same family of missed native op, and at (speed 3) SBCL emits an optimization
NOTE for each one it cannot open-code.  So the policy question has a second
payoff even if the policy itself does not ship: compiling the runtime at
(speed 3) once and reading the notes is a free census of the runtime's
generic-arithmetic and hairy-aref sites.

THE MEASUREMENT (probe tree: one declaim inserted after the first
`(in-package :pcl)`; A/B against the tree's own runtime, interleaved, min-of-3
â the machine was running a companion suite at the same time, so treat these
as directional, not final):

    arrhash   0.1578 -> 0.1496   -5.2 %
    oo        4.2414 -> 3.9666   -6.5 %
    feread    0.5567 -> 0.5389   -3.2 %
    numstr    0.5290 -> 0.5266   -0.5 %
    slices    0.5894 -> 0.6028   +2.3 %
    gcdrec    0.1635 -> 0.1828  +11.8 %

Three rows better by 3-6.5 %, one flat, two worse â and gcdrec's +11.8 % is on
a 0.16 s row measured under contention, so it may be noise or may be real (a
recursive sub is exactly where (speed 3)'s inlining decisions differ most).

WHAT TO DO, IN ORDER:
 1. re-run this A/B on a QUIET machine at K=5 or better, all bench rows;
 2. whatever the verdict, do a (speed 3) compile ONCE and harvest the
    optimization notes â the `%p-fixnum-string` class of bug is invisible
    at the default policy and loud at (speed 3);
 3. only then decide the policy.  Note it is not free either way: (speed 3)
    raises the runtime's own COMPILE time, which every core build pays, and
    the s462as run did not measure that.

DO NOT ship the declaim on these numbers.

================================================================
SHIPPED s463av (round 20 perf slot).  All three steps done; the declaim ships,
one real bug came out of the note harvest, and the compile cost is measured.

STEP (a) — THE A/B, ON ALL ROWS, K=5, SIX INTERLEAVED RUNS.
`tools/bench-exec.pl` gained a runtime A/B mode for this (BENCH_RT_B=<runtime>
builds a second core and times both PCL sides INTERLEAVED, one series' round-r
sample before any series' round-(r+1), so a load drift during a row hits all
series alike).  A = this file at the default policy, B = the same file with one
`(declaim (optimize (speed 3)))` after the first `(in-package :pcl)`.  Median
B/A over six runs, and the SIGN OF ALL SIX is what makes a row a verdict:

    feread    -7.2 %   (-3.4 -11.0 -12.9 -6.1 -6.7 -7.6)   all six negative
    arrhash   -5.2 %   (-4.1 -5.2 -6.3 +1.7 -5.2 -5.8)     five of six
    cfor      -5.0 %   (-6.6 -5.4 -4.6 -5.5 +2.2 -2.1)     five of six
    ovlsub    -3.9 %   (-1.5 -10.0 -7.6 -1.2 -3.4 -4.4)    all six
    feread2   -2.6 %   (-2.0 -3.5 -2.2 -4.1 -2.8 -2.4)     all six
    arrfill   -2.2 %   (-3.6 -1.8 -1.0 -2.6 -3.3 -1.8)     all six
    regexg    -2.1 %   slices -1.5 %   strcat -1.4 %       five/six of each
    intloop+= +0.8 %   intloop= -1.3 %  fib -1.2 %  gcdrec -1.2 %
    collatz    0.0 %   sliceasgn +0.1 % symref -0.0 % pack -0.4 % packunpk -0.5 %
                                                     (all sign-mixed = noise)

NO ROW IS CONSISTENTLY SLOWER.  **The s462as suspicion is killed by the data**:
gcdrec read +11.8 % on the K=3 loaded run and reads -1.2 % with mixed signs
over six samples.  It was load, not the recursive sub.  Loads recorded per run
(1-min average 0.6 to 4.9 — a sibling agent and the reviewer were live).

STEP (b) — THE NOTE HARVEST.  3179 notes; full census, the reproduction recipe
(a COMPILE-FILE in an image that has already loaded the runtime — `load` of a
source file emits no notes at all, which is why nobody had seen them), and the
residue with owners are in task **#983**.  Two things came out of it:

  * **#980, a real bug and the reason two bench rows could not be measured at
    all.**  `pack` at (speed 3) dies "cl/pcl-pack.lisp not found" on a file
    that is present: SBCL turns a defun's reference to its own name into a
    LOCAL call when (> speed debug), and the self-loading extension stubs
    delegate to a definition the extension installs OVER them.  `p-pack` and
    `p-unpack` were the two hand-written stubs; the `%pcl-def-ext-stub` macro
    (mro/warnings/xs) had always delegated through SYMBOL-FUNCTION.  Fixed,
    guarded by a source invariant, shipped in the same commit.
  * **248 of the 3179 notes were ONE missing declaration** — every
    `(funcall (p-magic-cell-getter v))`, inlined into `unbox`/`box-set`.  The
    slots are now `:type function` with erroring defaults.  Cold path, so no
    speed change: a declared invariant and 8 % of the census gone.

STEP (c) — THE COMPILE COST, which the s462as run did not measure.  Interleaved
best-of-3 saved-core builds:

    default policy   3.02 s      (speed 3)   4.11 s     +36.2 %
    core size 46.9 MB either way

Paid once per edit of this file (cores are content-keyed and cached under
~/.pcl-cache/core), and a PROGRAM's compile time is untouched — the
end-of-file declaim still governs that.  On `tools/prove-core` the extra 1.1 s
is under 1 % of the gate's wall time.

THE DECISION: SHIP.  Nine rows consistently faster by 1.4-7.2 %, none
consistently slower, +36 % on a cached once-per-edit compile, and the one
semantic hazard the policy carries (self-call conversion) found, fixed and
guarded.  Measured before shipping, not assumed: no other runtime function is
redefined by a loaded artifact (the four artifacts' defuns diffed against this
file's), and generated user code is unaffected — it already compiles at
speed 2 / debug 0, and a perl sub that recurses and is then redefined through a
glob still reaches the new body (probed against perl 5.40.3).

The declaim carries all of this as a comment at its own site, including the
instruction for the next person: if something here ever needs to be redefinable
at runtime, delegate through SYMBOL-FUNCTION rather than lowering the policy.
subject: Perf: the RUNTIME compiles at SBCL default policy â the only optimize declaim is at the END of the file (measure at speed 3, and harvest its notes)
